Definition: Gilad, a region East of the Jordan; also the name of three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: n pr loc Gilead = "rocky region"; 1) a mountainous region bounded on the west by the Jordan, on the north by Bashan, on the east by the Arabian plateau, and on the south by Moab and Ammon; sometimes called 'Mount Gilead' or the 'land of Gilead' or just 'Gilead'. Divided into north and south Gilead; 2) a city (with prefix 'Jabesh'); 3) the people of the region; n pr m; 4) son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh; 5) father of Jephthah; 6) a Gadite
